| 072-claude | P02/P45-family handoff: halve every residual-stream write (emb, attention proj, fc2) after pretraining, a function-preserving rescale | claude-opus-5-5 | init, optimizer | 0.3 | 1200/300/4 | 14 | 344 | 753 | discard | 0.988 | 0.0915 | 92 273 601 761 | 1073 | P02 follow-up handoff transform: halving every residual-stream write (emb, proj, fc2 weights+biases; RESID_SCALE 0.5) after the unchanged 070-claude pretraining scored 370/350/311 on seeds 0/1/2 versus 359/335/364: exact means 343.666667 versus 352.666667, -9.00 (-2.6%); paired +11/+15/-53. Discard; inside the registered -40 to +30 range. The rescale was NOT function-preserving in practice, which falsifies the registered drift prediction (<1e-2): the logged max \|logit drift\| on the first 128 val records was 1.68/1.61/2.05. The probe includes pad positions and does not separate them from real tokens, so where the drift sits is unmeasured. Leading (untested) suspect is LayerNorm eps 1e-5: halving the residual stream makes eps 4x larger relative to its variance, most at block 0's ln1 (embedding rows only) and at pad positions whose embedding never gets gradient. The drift hurt the start: round-1 targets 92/284/102 vs 200/324/206, round-1 sample acc 0.019/0.094/0.021 vs 070's 0.059 (s0) and 0.129 (s1). Pretraining itself matched 070: 4747/4754/4738 steps, final val loss 0.0915/0.0923/0.0942 vs 0.0911/0.0913/0.0961. RL then caught up fast, consistent with (but not proof of) higher RL plasticity. Targets went 92->273->601->761 on s0 (round-4 acc 0.435/0.474/0.395 vs 0.464/0.460/0.485) and RL-solved was 761/807/690 vs 788/783/838. Seeds 0/1 beat 070 on dev at every length (s0 ge 7/8/9/10 = 370/302/221/30 vs 359/281/201/20) and seed 2 did not recover (690 RL-solved, ge>=10 9 vs 27). Post-RL held-out greedy 0.988/0.9905/0.989 vs 0.987/0.987/0.9875. Totals 1073/1055/994 s vs 1048/971/1079, no timing cost. So this run confounds a damaged start with extra plasticity and cannot isolate the mechanism. Next: an exact version that also sets every LayerNorm's eps to eps*RESID_SCALE^2 at handoff (then the rescale is exact), checking drift on non-pad positions only before launch. |

| 076-claude | P23-family: squared-ReLU MLP activation (Primer) instead of GELU, parameter-identical | claude-opus-5-5 | architecture | 0.3 | 1200/300/4 | 14 | 320 | 769 | discard | 0.9825 | 0.0945 | 172 339 631 763 | 1079 | P23-family: squared-ReLU MLP, fc2(relu(fc1(h))^2), on the 070-claude incumbent scored 297/323/339 on seeds 0/1/2 versus 359/335/364: exact means 319.67 versus 352.67, -33.0 (-9.4%); paired -62/-12/-25. Discard; inside the registered -40 to +30 range but far below the central +3. The registered step prediction failed: pretraining ran only 3620/3657/3647 steps versus 070's 4784/4750/4776 (-24%, ~1.31x step time). Most likely cause (not profiled): relu and square are two unfused elementwise passes, with an extra saved intermediate, over the 128 x T x 1024 MLP hidden tensor where GELU is one fused kernel, and at d_model 256 these memory-bound ops are a large share of each step. Despite 24% fewer steps, final val loss matched 070 (0.0945/0.0908/0.0933 vs 0.0911/0.0913/0.0961; means 0.0929 vs 0.0928), so per step relu^2 learned faster, as in Primer, but per wall-clock second it bought nothing, and downstream RL was worse at matched val loss: RL-solved 763/762/781 vs 788/783/838, round-4 sample acc 0.434/0.435/0.463 vs 0.464/0.460/0.485. Sampling speed was not the problem: total seconds 1065/971/1079 vs 1048/971/1079, no timeout risk realized. The result confounds the activation with 24% fewer optimizer steps; separating them needs a fused relu^2 (e.g. a compiled MLP), and the matched-val-loss/worse-RL pattern means that is worth doing only if the step-time cost can be removed. |

The +48 exceeds the stated -25..+30 range; with one-seed sd ~44 part of it is likely luck. Two mechanisms are confounded here: the more uniform update spectrum (singular values ~[0.86,1.14] vs ~[0.68,1.13]) and a ~15% larger update RMS, which under the lr-coupled 10x decoupled decay also shifts the equilibrium weight norm. An RMS-matched control (Polar Express with MUON_LR / 1.15, or the old quintic scaled x1.15) would separate them. |

| 111-fable | NoPE: no positional encoding (rotary rotation of q and k removed in all six Peri-LN blocks) on the 107-claude Lean incumbent (4.80M params) | claude-fable-5-1 | architecture | 0.2 | 2400/300/4 | 27 | 547 | 990 | discard | 0.982 | 0.0825 | 556 776 914 1014 | 1467 | NoPE (rotary rotation of q and k removed from all six Peri-LN blocks, 4,800,000 params identical to 107) scored 559/505/576 on seeds 0/1/2 vs 107-claude's 582/571/608: exact means 546.67 vs 587.00, -40.3, every seed down (paired -23/-66/-32), inside the registered -60..+40 range but near its bottom (central -10). Discard. Two surprises. (1) Removing RoPE was a large systems win: 4716/4704/4706 pretraining steps vs 3264/3208/3277 (+44%, predicted +1-3%), and RL sampling 304-351 samples/s vs 194-249, so RL rounds took 201-229 s vs 266-322 s and totals were 1467/1406/1405 s vs 1946 (the fork's apply_rope is ~8 small strided ops per q and k per block, 12 calls per forward, and this launch-bound model pays for every one). The extra 44% steps bought no fit: final val loss 0.0825/0.0800/0.0848 vs 0.0822/0.0827/0.0836 (minima 0.0797/0.0767/0.0782, all rising into the endpoint), held-out greedy 0.982/0.983/0.978 vs 0.9815/0.977/0.9785, so a position-free model fits cap-6 Lean chains about as well as RoPE with no more sample efficiency. (2) The registered mechanism is not supported: the RL start was much worse, not better. Round-1 targets solved 556/568/464 vs 722/689/679, round-1 sample acc 0.232/0.248/0.139 vs 0.29 mean, L* 9/9/8 vs 10, even though round-1 parse failures were similar (11078/9519/15004 of 48,000, 24.7%, vs 12155/7575/17990, 26.2%). So NoPE samples parse as often but prove less at lengths 7+, i.e. the content-addressed-retrieval story did not transfer to unseen lengths; this matches 058's finding that a NoPE layer strengthened rather than weakened the cap-6 prior. RL recovered part of the gap (r4 solved 1014/959/998 vs 1089/1031/1083, mean +403 from r1 vs 107's +371) but not all; final eval greedy 0.987/0.986/0.992. Lesson for the loop: RoPE costs ~30% of pretraining wall-clock and ~35% of sampling throughput here, so a cheaper positional encoding that keeps RoPE's extrapolation behaviour (e.g. a fused/complex-multiply RoPE, or RoPE on fewer heads) could bank the steps without the NoPE penalty. |

Each block now builds a (B, 8, T, S) bias that requires grad, so SDPA cannot use the fused kernel and the bias build, cast and backward run six times per step; RL decoding was unaffected (238-316 samples/s vs 256-313; rounds 247-330 s; totals 1639/1832/1769 s). Omission: the registration promised a final-gate diagnostic (mean log f per head) that the code never logged, so the direction the gates moved (presumably steeper than the init slopes) is inferred from the collapse, not measured. Lessons: across 116-fable (T5-bucketed table, +3), 116-claude (learned per-block slopes, +3) and this run (-90), the positional heads' distance prior is at a local optimum under 115's fixed table: static reshaping buys nothing and content-dependence learned from cap-6 statistics hurts, so the next ideas should leave the positional mechanism alone. If content-dependent decay is ever retried it needs (a) a fused kernel (FlexAttention score_mod with a cumsum bias) and (b) a length-safe parametrisation, e.g. gates that can only OPEN relative to the ALiBi slope (log f >= -slope) so the decay can never exceed the fixed prior that 115 showed extrapolates. |

(1) Cost: the second float-mask SDPA per block plus the head norm cost 32% of pretraining steps, 2827/2851/2845 vs 4204/4218/4263, well outside the predicted 3,300-3,900 (-8% to -22%), and RL sampling fell to 187-232 samples/s from 256-313, rounds took 277-346 s and totals were 1947/1878/1934 s vs 1572 (under the 2,400 s cap); like the canon layers of 109, a few extra small kernels per block are expensive in this launch-bound model. (2) Fit stayed close despite a third fewer steps: final val loss 0.0819/0.0850/0.0840 vs 0.0826/0.0806/0.0792 (minima 0.0789/0.0746/0.0796, all rising into the endpoint), held-out greedy 0.9835/0.983/0.9785 vs 0.9815/0.983/0.9845, so per step the differential heads fit the cap-6 data faster, yet that fit gave a worse 7+-line start, the pattern 112 (parallel block) showed. The mechanism was used, not ignored: learned lambda after pretraining 0.16/0.46/0.59/0.63/0.67/0.60 (s0), 0.15/0.35/0.59/0.75/0.65/0.57 (s1), 0.18/0.43/0.58/0.64/0.68/0.65 (s2) vs init 0.20/0.36/0.47/0.56/0.62/0.67, inside the predicted 0.1-0.9, with blocks 1-4 subtracting more than at init, and RL raised every block further (s0 final 0.16/0.50/0.61/0.66/0.72/0.64). Open hypotheses for the loss: 16-dim maps have too little resolution at this width to place a cited premise uniquely, so the subtraction cancels signal as well as noise; or the subtraction calibrated on cap-6 contexts over-suppresses at unseen lengths, as the steep decays of 113 and 117-fable did. A 32-dim-map version needs 16 maps per block (+786k params) and would cost even more steps. Lean gate: 119,583 parse failures of 800,736 samples vs 106,190 for 115; Lean vetoed 0 nd_verify-accepted proofs, 3 Lean-accepted proofs were rejected by nd_verify. |

| 146-claude | Systems: pack each step's 128 records into ~64 document-masked rows instead of padding every record to the batch max (same batches, same math), spending the ~2x fewer token slots on more steps, on the 136-fable MTP Lean incumbent | claude-opus-5-5 | systems, batch | 0.45 | 2400/300/4 | 53 | 579 | 1051 | discard | 0.962 | 0.0886 | 438 849 974 1043 | 1635 | Systems speed idea falsified on its own measurement: packing the same 128 records per step into document-masked rows worked mechanically (packed_rows_mean 63.3/63.4/63.3, about half the 128 padded rows, as predicted) but the step rate FELL, 2430/2484/2230 pretrain steps vs 136-fable's 3370/3351/3367 (-28/-26/-34%; steady ~8.6 vs ~11.8 steps/s from the first curve point on, so not warm-up or allocator growth), against a registered 4400-5800. Metric 574/562/600 (mean 578.67) vs 658 (655/673/646): -79.3, paired -81/-111/-46, far below the registered 0 to +20. The loss math is identical to the padded layout (CPU check: loss equal to 1e-6, grad diff 7.7e-7), so this run is a clean fewer-steps ablation of the incumbent: ~29% fewer steps cost ~79 theorems. Post-pretrain held-out greedy 0.962/0.937/0.958 vs 0.965/0.9705/0.968; final val loss 0.0886/0.0860/0.0780 vs 0.0860/0.0833/0.0788; RL-solved targets after round 4 1043/1024/1085. Why slower is unprofiled. Two points (interpretation, not measured here): 103/124 moved MLP FLOPs by +-17% for only -+4-5% steps, so most of the step is per-block overhead (kernel launches, the unbatched Muon over 30 matrices) rather than tokens, and halving token slots saves little. And packing replaced the batch-broadcast (1,H,T,T) ALiBi bias, which torch 2.4 pads before expanding and which stays L2-resident, with a dense per-row (R,H,L,L) bias: a 170 MB float32 masked_fill plus an 85 MB bf16 copy per block, read from DRAM in every attention forward and backward. That per-row bias is the leading suspect for the ~33 ms/step added. Next speed work should cut launches, not tokens: batch the Muon Newton-Schulz by shape, or use CUDA graphs/compile over a few padded length buckets. Keep the broadcast bias. |

Lesson for the speed lane: on this pod image, compile only with a FIXED padded shape (pad every batch to constant T and constant record count, i.e. give up token-budget batching or pad to a small set of shapes and compile each once, ~50 s each), or upgrade the pod's torch before trying dynamic shapes; the throughput of a compiled step was never observed, so the lead is still unmeasured. Reading: ALiBi's linear bias makes the two sharp heads (slopes 1/4, 1/16) functions of the absolute gap size, and a head trained at mean gap 2 (P(gap=1) ~ 0.5) attends ~2x more broadly in tokens at test; Ruoss et al. 2023's gains came from encodings and tasks where only the ordering/relative range matters, and did not transfer to fixed-slope ALiBi at this scale. Expert iteration repaired most of it (2,400 AdamW steps at arange positions: round-4 solved 1127/1109/1161 vs 1157/1168/1191, metric_rl 1132 vs ~1172), so the -37 is mainly the weaker start compounding through fewer round-1/2 proofs (+467/+434/+574 vs 153's +1177 on seed 0). Steps 4260/4185/4159 (mean 4201 vs 4503, -6.7%; registered floor 4,200) look like a cost, but 149/160 saw ~8% pod-to-pod spread, so the randperm+sort cost is unmeasured. Positions are therefore not a free lever for 7-14-line transfer here; if anyone retries, keep gap 1 inside a local window (or leave the two sharp heads at arange) and stretch only the cross-line / mild-slope distances, and check held-out greedy on the bench first. |

The registered sampler falsifier fired on every seed: round-1 RL targets solved 651/276/86 (153: 766/747/694), round-1 sample acc 0.178/0.056/0.015 (153 seed 0: 0.271), and 21,114/29,688/31,374 of the 48,000 round-1 samples failed to parse (44/62/65%). Seeds 0/1 recovered to 4-6k parse failures by round 2 but stayed behind (round-4 solved 1112/1030 vs 1157/1168/1191); seed 2 never recovered (parse-fail 29,075/25,396/24,371 in rounds 2-4 and 36,611 of 70,912 at eval, round-4 solved 428, eval 182 with nothing above 10 lines). Pretraining itself landed inside or better than every registered band: n_params 9,557,760; steps 4477/4435/4456 (153: 4540/4479/4489, -1.5%; registered 4,400-4,750, so the per-head reshapes were free as predicted); epochs 3.96/3.92/3.94; final val 0.0826/0.0874/0.0790 (153: 0.088/0.087/0.089), min val 0.0793/0.0725/0.0779; last train CE 0.046/0.080/0.033 (153: 0.060); held-out greedy 0.9475/0.959/0.9605 (153: 0.9675; seed 0 below the 0.955 band, the only pretraining-side miss). RL sampling 211-357 samples/s, totals 1795/1620/1469 s. So this is the 159-fable/167-claude/168-fable3/169-fable pattern in its strongest form yet: an attention-side change that keeps greedy decoding (eval greedy 0.983-0.9875) and matches or lowers the loss, but wrecks T 0.8 sampling; 167-claude's 34-50% round-1 parse failures cost -13, here 44-65% cost -53 to -503, and the seed-to-seed spread (sd 250 vs the usual ~25) says the damage is a threshold effect, not a shift. Interpretation, not measured: per-head orthogonalization hands every head a full-norm rank-48 update every step, so a head whose gradient is near zero (unused, or already fitted) receives pure noise at the full Muon step under only 0.1 x lr per-step decay; whole-matrix orthogonalization implicitly gates such heads because their rows get a small share of the shared singular vectors. Noisy q/k in a few heads are harmless under greedy decoding, where the confident heads dominate, but once the sampler takes an off-greedy token the state is one where those heads inject garbage, and the proof stops parsing. Claims (1)-(2) (the per-head maps are the modular dual) are untested by this; claim (3), that equal per-head steps help the sampler, is falsified. Do not retry head-wise Muon without gating each head's update by its momentum norm (or a per-head trust ratio), and treat any change that raises round-1 parse failures above ~10k as a sampler regression regardless of loss. |

Diagnosis of the collapse, from lean_gate.jsonl parse_reasons: it is one failure, the tokenizer's 'unbound' (a term cites a name with no binding in scope). Parse failures were 39,557 / 131,666 / 139,548 of 266,912 samples (15% / 49% / 52%); 'unbound' alone was 10,856 / 20,269 / 24,970 of the 48,000 round-1 samples, fell on seed 0 to 4,333, 2,760, 2,215 in rounds 2-4, and stayed at 22,864 / 22,191 / 21,528 (seed 1) and 23,516 / 23,334 / 22,306 (seed 2), i.e. ~46% of all samples, through round 4 (eval: 35,185 and 29,968 of 70,912). The same numbers appear in earlier collapses I re-read from their gate logs: 195-fable seed 0 had unbound 19,312 then 24,393 / 23,405 / 22,931, its seed 1 21,947 / 22,367 / 22,197 / 19,699, while its healthy seed 2 went 14,158 -> 3,695 -> 3,442 -> 3,357; 193-fable seed 0 started the same way (22,068, 20,625) and escaped in rounds 3-4 (9,397, 3,808) to score 669. So an RL collapse in this table is bimodal and specific: about half of the 7+ line samples cite an unbound name, and 600 fine-tune steps either repair that by round 2-3 or never do; every other parse reason is under 3% in all runs. Interpretation, not established: the renaming changed nothing measurable in pretraining, so either it makes this name-binding failure harder for the fine-tune to repair (its only functional change at handoff is which embedding rows and logits the atoms use), or 2 of 3 seeds were unlucky in a lottery the incumbent family also plays (191's 12-seed line at 663-700 argues against pure luck; 188, 195 and 197, all mine and all changing the input or readout path, each lost seeds this way). Three seeds cannot separate these. What I would do next: treat round-1/round-2 'unbound' counts as the early indicator instead of round-1 targets solved, and test pretraining changes aimed at keeping cited names in scope beyond six lines. Scope note: no data, tokenizer, augmentation, RL or harness change; the renaming was a deterministic function inside the model's forward. Local checks before launch all passed (renaming equals a Python reference, exact equivariance under 5 atom permutations, cached decoding equals the full forward). Infrastructure: bench needed three A40 capacity retries; the three run pods and the bench pod were terminated by the runner (38.2/33.3/33.7 min, ~$0.86). |

Reading, not established on two seeds: hiding dead scopes from the content heads removes about half of the unbound citations a freshly pretrained model makes at 7+ lines, so part of that failure is citing into closed boxes, but one round of expert iteration teaches the incumbent the same thing, and the ~2.5-3k per pass that remain in every run are untouched by the mask (names never bound, or the pending `have` of the box being written; I still have no failing samples to tell which). This is the third result (with 190 and 191) where the round-1 harvest moved by hundreds and the metric did not: the metric is not limited by how RL starts. Where the mask could still matter is collapse protection (188/195/197 each lost seeds to unbound rates that never fell), which three healthy seeds cannot test. If anyone retries this: make the cached update cheap first (the state is five (1024, ~600) tensors and ~30 kernel launches per token; int64 full-width products and a clone per token are avoidable, and the update is a no-op unless the token is a bracket or `fun`), and put the falsifier on seconds per pass, not samples/s. Local checks before launch all passed (mask equals a stack-parser reference on 400 real records, cached decoding equals the full forward to 1.9e-6).
